title: Storefronts
tagline: I'm the one who changes both websites.
sticker: 81 site pages and features in two years
what: I run two brand websites: the product pages, the homepages, the guides and everything a customer clicks between finding a product and paying for it.
does: Build and refresh product pages for two brands
Design homepage sections, banners and landing pages for products, sales and events
Keep prices, stock and pre-order messages right across the catalog
Add buy buttons, option pickers and payment plans at checkout
Show shipping times, holiday cutoffs and delivery warnings
Run our own find-a-store map and site search
Keep release notes, warranty, returns and help pages current
Fix titles, redirects and slow pages, and back up and patch the sites

solved.problem: The store was paying for a rented retailer map and rented site search, and both were hard to fix when they went wrong.
solved.did: I built my own map from real purchase evidence, with a dealer list the team manages, and then my own search.
solved.ended: Both rented services are gone, and search answers in a fraction of a second.

solved.problem: A site full of old pages, missing titles and stale links hurts search and confuses customers.
solved.did: I audited the pages, gave every live page a proper title, retired the dead ones safely, and kept the old links pointing somewhere useful.
solved.ended: Every live page has a title, and the leftovers are cleared.

solved.problem: Every page on both sites lived only inside the store's own system, with no copy of our own.
solved.did: I exported all the page templates and put the landing pages and guides under version history.
solved.ended: We have our own copy, and I can search every page at once.

tools.name: Self-updating prices
tools.line: the pages read their prices from one source, so nobody retypes a price after a change. Used by me and the sales team.

tools.name: Retailer finder
tools.line: my own find-a-store map, with a dealer list behind it that customer service keeps up.

tools.name: Stock switch
tools.line: turns a whole batch of products to sold-out or pre-order at once, with an undo. Customer service asked for it.

worksWith: Leadership, customer service, the sales team, the warehouse, purchasing, accounting, a contract designer, an outside web developer.
story: New owners have a guide with two clear paths, links straight to each section, and a printable version that builds itself from the page. The paper copy always matches.
Owners needed one place to start after opening the box. I mocked up a small site for them, then built it as a landing page.
Customer service sent 42 notes before launch and 17 more after. I worked through every one, taking the guide from mock-up to live over a few months.
The guide sits alongside the product pages, warranty, returns and help pages I keep current on both sites. Customer service helped shape what a new owner sees.
credit: The job, plus the tools I built for it
